conflicts: 54178.509 cm^-1 (J=4) level: the measured lifetime 8.3 ns (Den Hartog et al. 2005) corresponds to a total decay rate of 1.2e8 s^-1, but NIST lists A = 2.1e8 s^-1 (accuracy E, older source) for the single line 184.575 nm to the ground level, so lifetime x sum(A) = 1.74. The NIST A value of that line is too large; the measured lifetime is kept

notes: NIST ASD already carries A values for 166 Pt I lines; of the 58 measured lines (Gough-Hannaford-Lowe 1982, Lotrian-Guern 1982) in the Kurucz list gf7800.all only 3 are missing from NIST and those are added here (derived from log gf with A = 0.66702 sigma^2 gf / (2J'+1)). Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second); for the 248.792 nm line the heavier isotope lies at higher frequency. The 199Pt-198Pt shift on the same line is 0.98(48) GHz (199Pt is radioactive, not listed under isotopes). 195Pt has I = 1/2: hyperfine entries have A only. Isotope abundances in percent; abundance_unc in percent. Second pass (2026-10-02): 58 odd-level lifetimes from Den Hartog et al., Astrophys. J. 619, 639 (2005), Table 1 (levels there carry the Blaise et al. 1992 energies, matched to the NIST levels within 0.04 cm^-1 (most within 0.02) and by J). Where Table 2 prints an explicit uncertainty it is used; otherwise the uncertainty is the paper's stated rule 'larger of 5 % or 0.2 ns'. The NIST A values of Pt I already come from this paper's Table 3, so no transition rates were added.
